relevance_note: Case report of a woman with arterial tortuosity syndrome whose genetic study 'was positive for a mutation in GLUT10' (variant not printed), plus her clinically affected sister.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short script from hand-chosen values and spans. Two in-scope people: the single unnamed patient (label 'patient') and her 21-year-old sister ('sister of patient', in scope as an affected relative; no genetic test reported for her, so no variant row). The patient's variant is given only as 'a mutation in GLUT10' (gene printed as GLUT10, the protein encoded by SLC2A10 per the Discussion); variant row kept with variant_original_string 'not reported'. Zygosity/inheritance not stated. Contradiction/inconsistency: the abstract says 'elongation of the aortic root' for the patient while the case text says 'elongation of the aortic arch' for both sisters; the Discussion says aortic root for the sister; both recorded as separate rows. The case-text sentence on kinking and coiling is broken by page residue ('MY709 A' and figure captions), so it is quoted as two separate spans, not joined. Pulmonary-artery stenosis was diagnosed at catheterisation 'at 2 years of age and then again at 16 years'; this is recorded as feature detail, not as onset of disease or age at diagnosis of ATS, which the paper does not give. Table 1 haemodynamic data (pulmonary systolic pressure 110 mmHg) is not dated to a specific study, so not used separately. 'perfusion scintigraphy was normal' recorded as excluded 'abnormal pulmonary perfusion scintigraphy' (whole investigation, nothing more specific excluded). Dyspnoea mapped to checklist 'respiratory distress or insufficiency' as observed (judgment call). Abstract's 'peculiar dysmorphism' not recorded as it may describe ATS in general. Unspecified 'skin findings ... typical of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome' not mapped to lax skin or any specific checklist skin/joint item. The sister's findings are attributed from the case and Discussion text; Figs 4 and 6 show her angiography.
